svg.aria-label: RouteKit, a routing engine for scene-based UIKit and SwiftUI apps (SwiftUI screens hosted in UIHostingController), shown with the README's Notes app on iPhone Duo and iPad: a Handoff queued at cold launch, denied while signed out and replayed after sign-in with the list beneath the note; the scene unfolding into a split view with its route intact; a SwiftUI compose window opened beside the note and reused; every window obscured when inactive; after a relaunch each window restored — the note first, then the compose draft; and sign-out swapping every window to Sign in and closing the compose windows. Swift 6, iOS 15+ and Mac Catalyst.
svg.title: RouteKit — the Notes app, end to end
svg.text: The Notes app, end to end — scene routing for UIKit & SwiftUI

g.text: compose closed by its termination policy
A Handoff arrives while the splash plays — RouteKit queues it.
The router denies the pending note; it stays in the queue.
Login replays the queue — the note opens with the list beneath it.
The same scene resizes into a split view — the route stays intact.
A Safari link opens “Groceries” — it lands in the open window, pushed over Trip plans.
Compose — a SwiftUI view in a UIHostingController — opens as a second window.
Every window is covered until the app is active again.
Each window comes back as it was — the note first, then the draft.
StateRestoring.restore(with:) · per scene · same auth state
Every window swaps to Sign in; the compose windows close.
Scene routing for UIKit & SwiftUI — iPhone, iPhone Duo, iPad & Mac
Queued intents · multi-window routing · auth-driven navigation · obscuration · state restoration
